Subject: Post-call: VectorCloud interop recap & AB sprint manifest

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the clear signal around the two things you want validated before procurement: 1) p95/p99 latency delta vs Hyperscaler X for our standard chat prompt mix; 2) sustained tokens/sec throughput at 1k concurrent sessions for your median request size.

Quick recap and proposed AB sprint (high level):
- Hypotheses to test
  * H1: Redwood's continuous batching + KV caching will deliver lower p95 for short-turn prompts (<=64 tokens) than Hyperscaler X when quantized to int8.
  * H2: Hyperscaler X sustains higher peak tokens/sec at batch sizes >= 64 on their optimized TPU path, but Redwood's batching policy yields better per-token cost at p95 targets.
- Priority metrics: p95 and p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec sustained over 5-minute windows, per-token cost estimate (USD/token).
- A/B plan (two arms)
  * Arm A — Redwood default runtime on instance type rwd-gpu-1 (int8 quantized model variant + prefix cache enabled).
  * Arm B — Hyperscaler X managed endpoint (their recommended config for comparable model) — VectorCloud to stand up.
- Test length: 3 x 10-minute sustained runs per arm, measured at 1k concurrent sessions (poisson arrival), with synthetic and replayed real traces (you mentioned 60/40 split).
- Deliverables: raw p95/p99 CSVs, tokens/sec time series, consolidated runbook with knobs tested and configuration used, and a short slide with conclusions.

Action items I need from VectorCloud by EOD Thu:
1) A single 1-hour shared window when your infra team can run the Hyperscaler X arm (we can orchestrate Redwood side to match).
2) A copy of the sample payload distribution (percentiles for prompt length and response length) or a replay trace.
3) Any security constraints for us running test traffic into your staging endpoints.

Attachments: throughput-probe-spec.xlsx (xlsx, 74KB) — draft probe spec with traffic pattern and measurement definitions.

Next: Jordan will own scheduling and run orchestration; Ben will own metrics collection and cost model; Monica will write the runbook and collate results. I'll follow up with a calendar invite once Alex confirms the window.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — that matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our infra side: 
- We'll run Hyperscaler X arm in our staging project (non-prod) but cannot expose internal IDs; we can provide a staging endpoint and ephemeral keys for the test window.
- Our median prompt size is ~78 tokens (per your schema), response median ~120 tokens — attaching the sample percentile table in the trace we'll send.
- Security: must use mTLS to the staging endpoint; we can provide certs. No external embedding of PII in test traces (we'll scrub).

We can allocate a 2-hour window on Thursday 2029-05-23 starting 10:00 AM PDT. That should be enough to run the three runs and a short warmup.

One ask: can you include p99.9 for the short-turn (<=64 tokens) slice? Our SRE is worried about tail behavior on spikes.

Alex

Great — thanks Alex, that window works for us. A few technical clarifications from the Redwood side and a tighter runbook outline so your SREs know what we'll execute:

- Measurement specifics (we'll include these in the runbook):
  * p95/p99/p99.9 computed on server-side response-complete timestamps (not client-side).
  * Tokens/sec measured as emitted tokens/sec aggregated across the 5-minute steady-state windows; we'll report one-second granularity series.
  * Tail slices: we'll report dedicated metrics for short-turn <=64 tokens and long-turn >256 tokens.
- Config parity: we'll match model family and sequence-length cap where possible. For quantization, Redwood arm will run int8 and float16 as two subruns (int8 primary). If you can match with Hyperscaler X recommended quantized config, include that as a variant.
- Cost model: we'll attach our per-token cost calc; note this will be a Redwood estimate (we'll include assumptions).

Run timeline (Thu 2029-05-23, 10:00–12:00 PDT):
  10:00–10:20 Warmup (both arms)
  10:20–10:35 Arm A run 1 (10 min steady state + buffer)
  10:45–11:00 Arm B run 1
  11:10–11:25 Arm A run 2
  11:35–11:50 Arm B run 2
  11:55–12:05 Buffer / quick sanity checks / collect logs

Please confirm: (1) mTLS certs will be delivered by 08:00 Thu; (2) replay trace file or percentile table by EOD Wed; (3) a named contact from your infra team for handoff during the window.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-summary.pdf (pdf, 320KB) — internal summary slides with suggested config parity. Also including manifest-ab-runbook.md (md, 6KB) as a draft runbook.

I'll send calendar invites and a short ops channel (temporary Slack) for live troubleshooting.
